test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A dealer allowed a 32% discount on an article and was still able to manage a 57% profit. Find the ratio of the cost price to listed price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct Formula: Ratio of CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%)

Given: Discount = 32% and Profit = 57%

⇒ CP : MP = (100 − 32) : (100 + 57)

⇒ CP : MP = 68 : 157

**∴ The correct answer is 68 : 157.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount allowed = 32%

Profit earned = 57%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b5486737ed7d128ae61f9b8ec621c3c320f170f33d85e5adb9de28ab1a6cab4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price be CP and Listed Price (Marked Price) be MP.

⇒ SP = CP × (100 + 57)/100 = 157CP/100

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − 32)/100 = 68MP/100

⇒ Equating the Selling Price: 157CP/100 = 68MP/100

⇒ 157 × CP = 68 × MP

⇒ CP/MP = 68 / 157

⇒ CP : MP = 68 : 157

**∴ The correct answer is 68 : 157.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP-MP Relation

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is given by CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, Net Discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100. Always calculate profit or loss percentage on the Cost Price unless specified.
